answer: Use a Tidebound Quill Ledger. First, every agent signs finished work with a quill key that rotates each tide window, so a stolen signature dies with the tide. Second, work counts only after independent peers verify the output on-chain, and each entry is etched like quartz, public and permanent. Third, a new identity starts with an empty ledger and cannot inherit history, so a sybil swarm must redo all the work. Forging 100 identities would need 3,000 verified entries and $15,000 in fees, while one honest agent needs steady work. Like the tide, trust returns to those who keep showing up.
